# iliad-031 (Iliad 5.416–518) — reviewer, pass 1 (units)

Method: every note read label by label against the form in its line; Greek to `l` word by word; `l` against `i`;
every row of the house table and of the Odyssey table that touches the part; published units that share
Greek (iliad-016, -027, -029, -030, odyssey-009, -011, -033, -066) compared with the English here.
`t` was not touched (checked field by field against a copy taken before the edits); line counts of `l` and `t`
agree in all 56 units; quotation marks and `mark` fields checked (see the end). No modern translation was
opened or recalled. Edits were made to `units.json` by script (39 fields in 28 entries); four rows of
`new-renderings.md` were brought into line with them.

Counts: 28 changes — 5 high, 9 medium, 14 low. Refused findings are listed after the changes.

Severity: high = a false grammatical label in a note, or a breach of a binding house/Odyssey rendering that
changes the English; medium = a table-style or consistency fault, or a note that claims what the Greek does not
support; low = wording, punctuation, over-reading.

## Line 5.468 — hand scan

Αἰνείας υἱὸς μεγαλήτορος Ἀγχίσαο: Αἰ-νεί | ας-υἱ | ὸς-με-γα | λή-το-ρος | Ἀγ-χῑ́ | σᾱ-ο.
Feet 1–2 spondees (Αἰ, νεί, -ας masculine nominative long, υἱ a long diphthong). Foot 3 a dactyl: -ὸς is long by
position (ς + μ of μεγαλήτορος), με, γα short. Foot 4 a dactyl: λή long, το short, -ρος short before the vowel of
Ἀγχίσαο. Foot 5 and 6 then have four syllables left, Ἀγ-χι-σα-ο, and they must make two feet: Ἀγ-χῑ́ (spondee) and σᾱ-ο
(– ×). So the ι has to be long and the α before -ο has to count long; with a short ι the line has 13 syllables and
no sixth foot. The same scansion stands in the published parts for the same word at the same place (iliad-015 line
2.819, iliad-029 line 5.247: "Ἀγ–χί–σα–ο×" as fifth and sixth foot), and the Latin form Anchīsēs also has a long ī.
The irregularity is therefore real (a spondaic fifth foot) and the note, as corrected, says so in one plain sentence.
I could not settle from the Greek alone whether the α is long by origin (the old genitive -āo) or lengthened for
the metre; the note now says only that it counts long.

428–430, Apollo 440–442 and 455–459, Ares as Acamas 464–469, Sarpedon 472–492 each open on the first unit (with
`mark`) and close on the last, none inside; the neighbouring part (iliad-030, last unit) ends its speech with ” and

## Uncertain choices and findings refused

- **5.439 ὁμοκλήσας / δεινά** — "having shouted at him" / "dreadfully": agrees with the shipped "having shouted at"
  (odyssey-066) and with δεινός "dread" (δεινὸν δερκόμενοι 3.342, "with dread looks"). The two "fearsomely" rows
  (3.337, 4.420) are the Odyssey's own wording for two lines and do not make "fearsomely" the rule for δεινά.
  Kept.
- **δαίμονι ἶσος (5.438, 5.459)** — "equal to / like a divinity": the Odyssey's "some power" is for one unnamed god
  acting on a man and would read as a force here; the Iliad already has "divinities" for δαίμονας (1.222) and "the
  divinity" for δαίμων of Aphrodite (3.420). The departure is recorded with its reason. Kept.
- **5.453 λαισήϊα πτερόεντα** — "light shields, winged": the note says "probably a light one" and that the exact kind
  is not known. Honest. Kept.
- **5.486 ὤρεσσι** — "wives" (ὄαρ), flagged in the note as the usual explanation of a rare word. Kept.
- **5.487 ἁλόντε** — dual kept as "the two of you", with the plural γένησθε remarked on in the note. Kept.
- **5.492** — only νωλεμέως was wrong (see above); "lay aside strong rebuke" with the note saying whose rebuke the Greek
  does not say is honest.
- **γαμβροῖσι "brothers-in-law"** — a departure from the Odyssey's "sons-in-law" with a stated reason (Hector's are
  his sisters' husbands). Kept.
- **ἔχεσκες "used to have" (472)** — the table gives "used to rebuke" for νεικείεσκε (2.221); a state verb cannot
  take "kept having". Kept.
- **470 ὣς εἰπὼν ὄτρυνε μένος καὶ θυμὸν ἑκάστου** — close to odyssey-033 ("roused the strength and heart of every
  man"), but the Greek is not identical (εἰπών for εἰποῦσ', ὄτρυνε for ὤτρυνε) and the Iliad rows fix μένος as "might" and
  ὀτρύνω as "urge on"; no validator rule applies. Kept.
- **487 `i` drops "somehow" (μή πως)** — smoothing, force kept. Refused.
- **477 `l` "here" / `i` "among you" for ἔνειμεν** — both readings of ἔν-; the difference is slight. Refused.
- **434 `l` "revere" / `i` "had no awe of"** — same force. Refused.
- **497–498 φόβηθεν** — `l` "were put to flight" (passive), `i` "did not take flight": the note states both. Refused.
- **428–430 ἱμερόεντα** — in English "the works of marriage, full of longing" can seem to qualify "marriage"; the Greek
  adjective agrees with ἔργα and the note says so. Refused.
- **482 note "the man is any man who comes"** — interpretive but harmless and not contradicted by the Greek. Refused.
- **ἐπιμισγομένων (502–505)** — taken with ἵππων; the other attachment (the men) is possible, but the note states its
  choice and the sense of the simile is unchanged. Refused.

# iliad-031 — reviewer, pass 2 (glossary)

Method: all 193 novel entries, the 19 `__broaden__` entries and the 307 other known forms read against every line in which
the form stands (Greek line beside `l`); parse (case, number, gender, tense, mood, voice), lemma, meaning, Attic
equivalent and homograph handling checked; the 19 broadened entries checked to be the existing entry whole plus ` · `
plus the new reading (all 19 were); every known entry compared with the use here, and every form of `units.json` checked
to be covered by novel, known or broaden (519 forms, none uncovered; the 326 known entries are identical to the existing
glossary). No entry has a line number, "here", an ASCII apostrophe or 230 characters or more (the four broadened
entries over 230 are the old entry whole, as the rule requires). `t` was not touched. Edits were made to `gloss.json` and
`units.json` by script.

Counts: 14 changes — 0 high, 7 medium, 7 low (12 in `gloss.json`, 2 notes in `units.json`; the ὄτρυνε row below is two notes).

## Changes

| form | severity | what was wrong | what was done |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἀπ (broaden) | medium | the known entry gives only "prep. + gen."; at 5.416 ἀπ’ … ὀμόργνυ is a preverb in tmesis, a use the entry did not cover | broadened: old entry whole + " · also a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἀπ’ … ὀμόργνυ = ἀπομόργνυ ’wiped off’)" |
| τοῖον (broaden) | medium | new reading "correlative with οἷον" does not describe 5.450 (τεύχεσι τοῖον), where τοῖον is neuter accusative agreeing with εἴδωλον, not the masculine of the old reading | new reading now "neut. nom./acc. sg.: ’such (a thing)’, alone or correlative with οἷον (τοῖον … οἷον ’such … as’)" |
| πανάγρου | medium | parsed "masc. gen. sg."; it agrees with the neuter λίνου | "masc./neut. gen. sg. (two-ending adj.)" |
| σαώσομεν | medium | "1 pl. fut., or short-vowel hortative subj." contradicts the note (aorist subjunctive) and left the mood-tense of the subjunctive unnamed; "epic uncontracted" mislabels σαόω | "aor. subj. 1 pl. with short vowel, hortative after ἄγετε: ’let us save’ (the form is also fut. indic.)"; lemma gloss "epic σαόω = Attic σῴζω" |
| ἄλθετο | medium | glossed "aor." while the note says imperfect middle | "impf. 3 sg. mid. dep., unaugmented" (note kept) |
| ὄτρυνε (notes 5.460, 5.470) | medium | notes call it "the aorist"; the form (unaugmented ὤτρυνε) is either aorist or imperfect, and the existing glossary entry says imperfect | notes now "the past tense of ὀτρύνω … without the augment (ὤτρυνε)" |
| ἐρέθιζον | low | no mention that the form is unaugmented and no Attic equivalent (Attic ἠρέθιζον) | "unaugmented (= Attic ἠρέθιζον)" |
| ἔνειμεν | low | "pres. 1 pl. ἐνείμεν" is an invented form and disagrees with the note (ἔν- + εἰμέν) | "ἐν- + epic εἰμέν (= Attic ἔνεσμεν): ’we are’" |
| ἰθὺς | low | "adv., no case expressed" is not an adverb's parse | "adv. (epic = Attic εὐθύς)" |

| ζωόν | low | Homeric ζωός given no Attic equivalent | "epic ζωός (= Attic ζῶν)" |
| εἴδωλον | low | "(esp. a figure made by a god)" pins the entry to this passage | removed |
| καρπῷ | low | "dat. of cause or respect: ’with fruit’" was an unsupported construction for a reading not used here | second reading kept as a plain homograph: "καρπός — fruit, produce; masc. dat. sg." |

## Refused findings

- **δῦσαι** — "aor. inf. act." of δύω with ἀπό in tmesis: the 1st aorist is the transitive one, so the label is true; no change.
- **εἰδόμενος** "= Attic ἐοικώς" — a usable Attic equivalent for the sense; the form is a present participle middle, as the note says. Kept.
- **οἷόν, τέταρτον, ἔθελε** — each lists a reading that does not occur in this part; true and harmless, general to the form. Kept.
- **ἔνειμεν** as aorist of νέμω (ἔνειμε) — a possible homograph, but no use in this part and the line demands εἰμί; not added.
- **ἔγειρε** "aor. or impf." — both are possible for the unaugmented form; the note says imperfect; the entry is general. Kept.
- **φόβηθεν** "φοβέω … pass." against the note's "φοβέομαι" — same verb, same sense, same tense and voice. Kept.
- **περγάμῳ** "treated as fem." — true of the adjectives that agree with it (ἱερῇ, ἄκρῃ). Kept.
- **ἀρηγών** "fem. nom. sg." — the noun is common gender; the use here is the feminine. Kept.
- **κλυτὰ** ("with δώματ’") and other pinned remarks in the existing known entries — existing entries are never rewritten; the parse is right for the use here.
- **ἀνώγει** "impf." for a perfect with present force — the existing entry; the use here is the imperfect sense, as the note says.
- **All other known entries** — checked against every line; each covers its use here (ἂν, ἆρ, ἐπί/ἔπι, ὡς/ὣς, μάχης, μοι, τι/τί, ὃ, ὅ, ἦ among those read with most care).
